references.text: Israel is described as a stiff-necked people, the same characteristic Moses uses here to describe their rebelliousness.
The Lord calls Israel a stiff-necked people after the golden calf incident, showing their repeated rebelliousness.
Moses acknowledges that the people are stiff-necked and asks for forgiveness for their wrongdoings.
Moses reminds the people that they have been stubborn against the Lord from the day he knew them.
Moses says that the people have been stubborn against the Lord as long as he has known them.
The psalm describes the fathers as a rebellious and defiant generation, who did not keep their hearts steadfast.
The Lord says that He knew Israel was stubborn, with an iron-hard neck, reflecting Moses' words.
Ezekiel is sent to a rebellious people who have risen up against the Lord, similar to Moses' description.
Stephen calls his listeners stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, always resisting the Holy Spirit.
